title: Stabilize routing convergence after stale route snapshots caused cascading downgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-26 we observed a capacity incident where smart-routing began downgrading traffic en masse to smaller, lower‑quality model variants across multiple regions. Unlike previous fallback loops, this event amplified because routing snapshots diverged between control-plane replicas and the circuit-breaker hysteresis allowed repeated downgrade decisions for the same request streams. Impact: several customer routes experienced elevated error rates and 3–5x token-cost increases due to repeated retries and fallbacks; latency SLOs were violated for ~35 minutes in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Root cause hypothesis: staggered policy propagation (route snapshot hash drift) + probe misclassification of variant compatibility triggered aggressive downgrade path; circuit-breaker window logic (hysteresis) was too permissive and kept re-tripping while replicas had different view of capacity. This ticket tracks investigation, short-term mitigation, and long-term hardening to prevent recurrence.
comments: 2026-02-26: Incident detected by synthetic monitors and alerted via PagerDuty at 15:12 UTC. Initial triage pointed to increased fallback rates in smart-routing. - Jordan L.

2026-02-26: Emergency rollback of recent routing policy propagation change was scoped but not required; we applied an emergency throttle on cross-region failover at 15:34 UTC which stabilized traffic while we gathered traces. - Aisha P.

2026-02-27: Post-incident telemetry collected: routing snapshot divergence correlated with policy-mesh update batches. Captured example request traces and router decision logs (trace ids attached in links). - Eng oncall

2026-03-01: Engineering sync: reproducer created in staging that simulates staggered policy propagation and circuit-breaker timing mismatch. Workstream split into 3 tracks: detection/telemetry, short-term guardrails, and protocol-level hardening. - Jordan L.

2026-03-04: Design review for new convergence guardrail (route-version handshake) completed; agreed to add route-version checks to decision path and make downgrade idempotent within a short window. - PM and Infra leads
2026-03-08: Initial PR for conservative hysteresis tuning and a faster KV-cache invalidation landed (PR #5921). Running canary in us-west-2 with shadow traffic. - Marco R.

2026-03-12: Canary looks stable for 48h; moving to runbook updates and expanding rollout. Remaining items: implement route-version handshake and add deterministic downgrade circuit-breaker. - Jordan L.
action_items: Jordan Lee: Implement route-version handshake in router decision path so routers refuse to act on fallbacks derived from stale snapshots. Estimate: 5 pts. Due: 2026-03-18.
Marco Ruiz: Add deterministic idempotent downgrade token and shorten circuit-breaker hysteresis window; add unit/integration tests. Estimate: 3 pts. Due: 2026-03-12.
Sofia Mendes: Add cross-replica snapshot divergence metric and an alert when >1% of active routers have mismatched route-hash. Estimate: 2 pts. Due: 2026-03-10.
Infra team: Implement a two-phase propagation (announce then commit) for policy mesh to avoid mid-propagation decisions. Coordinate with rollout owners. Estimate: 8 pts. Due: 2026-04-01.
Oncall playbook update: Document emergency throttle for cross-region failover and steps to revert recent policy rollouts. Owner: Ops. Due: 2026-03-09.
QA: Add reproducible e2e test that injects delayed policy propagation and validates no repeated downgrades across 10k requests. Owner: QA. Estimate: 3 pts. Due: 2026-03-20.
resolution_summary: Short-term: applied throttle on cross-region failovers and tuned circuit-breaker hysteresis which reduced amplification within 30 minutes. Medium-term: landed conservative hysteresis change and KV-cache invalidation PR; canaries show stability. Long-term: route-version handshake and two-phase policy propagation planned to ensure convergence and prevent stale-snapshot-triggered cascading downgrades. Monitoring added to detect snapshot divergence and fallback amplification.
